intended_object: The positive cosine operator cos Θ(U,V) of the operator angle between closed subspaces U and V of a Hilbert space, acting on U. It is the operator (P_U P_V P_U |_U)^{1/2} = |P_V|_U|. This comes from the docstring "positive cosine acting in source coordinates" and the module docs (Davis–Kahan spectral-cutoff argument).
explanation:
The body takes the modulus |W| = (W*W)^{1/2}, computed with the continuous functional calculus, of the canonical intertwiner W = P_V P_U + P_{V⊥} P_{U⊥}. It then restricts |W| to U, which is legitimate because |W| commutes with P_U.

W*W = P_U P_V P_U + P_{U⊥} P_{V⊥} P_{U⊥}, and this operator is block diagonal for H = U ⊕ U⊥. The square root of a block-diagonal positive operator is block diagonal, so the restriction of |W| to U is (P_U P_V P_U|_U)^{1/2}. That is |P_V ∘ ι_U|, the standard positive cosine cos Θ of the angle from U to V. This is exactly the intended object.

The definition works over ℂ only, while the underlying `modulus` and `spectraCanonicalIntertwiner` are available for any RCLike field. Still, the whole file and the Davis–Kahan paper it follows work with complex Hilbert spaces, which is the standard setting for this operator theory. The object is also a specific construction used inside this proof development, so I do not count the restriction to ℂ as a real narrowing. Mathlib has no definition of the cosine operator between subspaces.
